messages:
alex: quick follow-up on MHA layout ABI — we need to finalize the padding/stride contract before landing the kernel selector. question: should kernels assume packed QKV (contiguous in last dim) or operate on three separate tensors? also: alignment requirements and pad semantics for seq % block != 0.

tanya: +1 on locking this down. my preference is an explicit ABI where runtime passes: layout=(NHWC|NCHW), qkv_packed=(true|false), elem_bytes, stride_q/stride_k/stride_v, pad_len, alignment. keeps kernel code deterministic.

sam: concern: that API explodes argument list and coupling. alternative is enum variants (PACKED_NHWC, SEPARATE_NCHW, ...). enum is compact, but every new micro-layout forces adding variants. tradeoff: explicit vs. versioned enums.

alex: good point. also note kv-cache interactions: contiguous QKV simplifies slice offsets when we append to cache — single base + constant offsets per head. separate tensors mean three pointers per cache entry.

mira: from perf runs: contiguous packed QKV tends to improve L2 prefetch / vector loads for fused qkv matmul kernels, but some CUDA kernels that assume planar Q,K,V interleaving get ~8-12% better when Q,K,V are separate due to coalesced loads along different strides. so wins flip depending on head dim and warp mapping.

infra-bot: note: perf nightlies for branch 'mha-layout-abicontract' scheduled 2026-02-18 03:00 UTC.

alex: proposing a minimal runtime->kernel contract: runtime still normalizes tensors to a tiny descriptor struct and passes pointer+strides+meta. that is:

```
struct MhaLayoutABI {
  uint8_t layout; // 0=NHWC, 1=NCHW
  uint8_t qkv_packed; // 0=separate,1=packed
  uint16_t reserved;
  uint32_t elem_bytes;
  uint32_t stride_q;
  uint32_t stride_k;
  uint32_t stride_v;
  uint32_t pad_seq; // padded sequence length in elems
  uint32_t alignment; // alignment in bytes (64|128)
};
```

alex: kernels then check that strides are multiples of alignment and that pad_seq % block == 0 for their preferred block size. if not, runtime must either re-pad or fall back to generic gather-based kernel.

tanya: agree. default alignment should be 64B to match cache lines, but we should allow 128B for platforms where tensor cores / loads benefit. elem_bytes drives the alignment semantics (e.g., f16=2 bytes -> 32 lanes per 64B). document this clearly.

sam: for quantized paths (int8/4-bit), the ABI needs to include a compression tag and per-row scale pointer or a flag indicating packed bitwidth. otherwise kernel selection will be wrong. add small field: quant_type (0=none,1=int8,2=4bit).

mira: also a runtime note: when qkv_packed=true, we must define the packing order. proposal: [head][seq][3][head_dim] vs [seq][3][head][head_dim]. pick one and document. my vote: [seq][3][head][head_dim] for easier cache-friendly seq slices.

alex: agreed on explicit packing order. add a packing_enum to ABI. runtime will transform to that canonical form when handing off to kernels — transformation cost should be accounted in selector.

sam: selector logic idea:
- if layout supported and alignment ok and quant matches => pick fast fused kernel
- else if layout match but pad not aligned => runtime re-pad to aligned length if cheap, otherwise pick slower generic kernel
- else => generic reference kernel

mira: add perf guard: if runtime repad causes >1.5x memory temp spike vs slow path, prefer slow path. we don't want OOM spikes.

alex: action items:
- runtime: produce MhaLayoutABI struct and canonical packing conversion (alex)
- kernels: implement fast path checks for abi fields and add clear failure reason logs (mira, sam)
- perf: run matrix (head_dim x seq_len x qkv_packed flag) and post results (infra-bot scheduled)

tanya: ack. i'll draft a small RFC blurb summarizing ABI + packing enum and include microbench results.

sam: noted. i will add quant_type to the struct and a clause for fallback semantics.

mira: i'll prototype the fast kernel checks and a fallback gather kernel. should be quick.

alex: thanks team. if no objections by EOD I'll land the ABI PR and the selector shim. :thumbsup:

mira: :thumbsup:

sam: LGTM
